page: Microsoft Azure E48ads_v5 is an EADSv5-family virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor. Operating on the x86_64 architecture under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this server features 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 24 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The processor runs at a speed of 3.525 GHz. It is equipped with 384.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is bundled as a 1843 GB local disk, and the instance is capable of utilizing Premium Storage. No GPUs are present on this server.

Benchmark results indicate strong CPU and memory capabilities. The server achieves top-tier performance in stress-ng single-core and multi-core tests, alongside a high PassMark CPU score of 51437.1. Multi-threaded decompression via bzip3 is also strong at 245.66 GB/sec. Memory performance is supported by a strong PassMark memory score of 2931.27, though large-block memory read and write bandwidths fall within the average range at 94.97 GB/sec and 45.98 GB/sec respectively. For specialized tasks, the server demonstrates strong performance in image processing and ray tracing, while database operations, static web serving, and software compilation fall into the average category.

Given its high memory density of 8.0 GB per vCPU and integrated 1843 GB local storage, the E48ads_v5 offers a resource-dense profile suitable for memory-intensive workloads. The combination of dedicated AMD EPYC cores and substantial RAM makes it a viable option for large-scale databases, memory-cached applications, and enterprise workloads requiring local scratch space. It is appropriate for relational database management systems, data analytics, and memory-bound simulation tasks.
